'''Classic''' is a constructed format on [[GEMP]] (code <code>classic</code>). Its card pool is the same as [[Open]], with three banned icons.<ref name="gemp" /> [[Scott Lingrell]] ran a Classic Format playtest at [[DecipherCon 2002]].<ref name="dcon2002" /> The Players Committee made Classic an official format for all sanctioned events on 31 March 2003.<ref name="pc-classic03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030824053912/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/classicnews03312003.htm Classic Format Contest Results are In!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 August 2003.</ref>

* '''Designed by:''' [[Scott Lingrell]]<ref name="dcon2002" />
* '''Type:''' constructed
* '''GEMP:''' ''Classic'' (<code>classic</code>)

The card pool is Decipher-printed set ids 1&ndash;14 ([[Premiere]] through [[Theed Palace]]) and premium ids 101&ndash;112. It also includes current Virtual Sets 0&ndash;27 (ids 200&ndash;227) and the Virtual Premium Set (id 301). Cards with the Defensive Shield, Episode I or Maintenance icon are banned.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="sets" />

== Deck size ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Default deck size on [[GEMP]]
| 60 cards
|}
The GEMP format definition sets no deck size, so GEMP uses its default of 60 cards.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="lib-ec48dc19" />

== Players Committee definition ==
The Players Committee ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) lists Classic among its closed environment formats. Players build constructed decks from any Decipher cards or Virtual Cards (Legacy or Standard, depending on the event), except:<ref name="afg" />
* any card, including Defensive Shields, with an Episode I icon. The guide notes that ''Desperate Times'' has been clarified not to have the Episode I icon, so it is legal.
* any maintenance card, for example ''Blizzard 4'' or ''Lando Calrissian, Scoundrel''.
The GEMP definition also bans every card with the Defensive Shield icon.<ref name="gemp" />

== Players Committee history ==
The first Classic Format event was a non-sanctioned playtest tournament at [[DecipherCon 2002]] on Friday 1 November 2002, run by [[Scott Lingrell]] to gauge players' acceptance of the format; [[Drew Scott]] won it and $35.<ref name="pc-dconwrap">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424052656/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/dconwrapup.htm DecipherCon 2002], Andrew Howard (Tournament Support Advocate), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref> The Players Committee had announced the playtest on 29 October 2002 for 7pm. Legal cards were any produced by Decipher and Virtual Sets 1–3, except cards with the Episode I icon and the banned [[Never Tell Me The Odds]], [[3,720 To 1]], [[Scanning Crew]], [[Watch Your Step / This Place Can Be A Little Rough]] and any card with a Maintenance Cost. Entry was $5, the winner was to receive 80% of the entry fees, and everyone who took part was to get prizes.<ref name="pc-oct02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/october02archives.htm October Updates], swccgpc.com (29 October 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423222342/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/october02archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> Over the winter the Players Committee ran a Winter Classic Contest for tournament directors and players. Tournament directors who ran Classic Format events between 14 December 2002 and 31 January 2003 sent reports to the Classic Format Subcommittee by 7 February 2003. The reports were judged on creativity, attendance, number of events and overall presentation, and the results were to be announced on 15 February.<ref name="pc-jan03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/january03archives.htm January Updates], swccgpc.com (28 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030612020737/http://swccgpc.com:80/Archives/january03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 31 March 2003 it announced the winners (1st [[Jacob Taylor]] of San Marcos, Texas; 2nd [[Christian Kriesel]] of Madison, Wisconsin; 3rd [[David Kangas]] of Brush Prairie, Washington) and that, "effective immediately, Classic Format will be considered an official format for all sanctioned events", including the Championship Circuit, with a Classic Format Subcommittee reviewing the ban list; Virtual Set 5 was to include two alternative Starting Effects aimed at Classic.<ref name="pc-classic03" /> The contest prizes were Limited Premiere Rare, Uncommon and Common uncut sheets for 1st to 3rd, and every tournament director who sent in a report received a set of Episode I tournament foils.<ref name="pc-classic03" /> The first official ban list (31 March 2003) banned all cards with an Episode 1 icon, all cards with a maintenance cost, all "insert" cards and Watch Your Step / This Place Can Be A Little Rough.<ref name="pc-classicban">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030413134208/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/classicbanlist.htm SWCCG Classic Format Ban List], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 April 2003.</ref> In its "Player's Committee Update" column for ''[[Scrye]]'', posted on 8 April 2003, the Committee wrote that new virtual Starting Effects and Defensive Shields might also be introduced for Classic.<ref name="pc-scrye0408">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/scryenews04082003.htm Star Wars CCG Player's Committee Update], Josh Radke, swccgpc.com (8 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030417234016/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/scryenews04082003.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

The 30 October 2002 forum announcement of the playtest, signed by [[Andrew Howard]] as Player Advocate – Tournament Support, described the format's premise as taking players back to the "glory days" of SWCCG, before the newer, more powerful strategies were introduced, and said Classic might become part of the next year's Championship Circuit.<ref name="pcf-9-23">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23#23 SWCCG Player's Committee to Debut "Classic Format"], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 October 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041228093720/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=9 Internet Archive]</ref> On 7 December 2002 Howard opened a Classic Format forum on the Players Committee message board for discussing the format's rules and restrictions and ideas for "classic only" virtual cards, calling Classic an experiment in organized play.<ref name="pcf-368-5190">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5190#5190 Classic Format Forum Open for Discussion!], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041217215720/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5190%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> The same day he announced the Classic Format "Winter Celebration" contest, open to tournament directors and Squadron Members. Its base rules made all cards produced by Decipher and the Players Committee legal except cards with the Episode I icon, [[Watch Your Step / This Place Can Be A Little Rough]], all characters with permanent weapons, [[Brangus Glee]] / [[Ketwol]], cards with a maintenance cost and "insert" cards. Tournament directors could add their own restrictions to test improvements to the format; Howard wrote that the restrictions applied only during the testing phase, and he expected that, if the format succeeded, Classic would get its own Virtual Cards to fix the problems that made them necessary. Contest tournaments had to be posted, and their results entered, on Decipher's tournament site, which made it the first time Classic was available as a sanctioned format (it was entered in the tournament software as "Scenario"). The announcement planned to name the top three on 7 February 2003; besides the three Limited Premiere uncut sheets (Light or Dark Side, at the winner's choice), two Honorable Mention prizes were to go to the tournament directors with the largest turnout and the best report. Howard called Classic "still a possible addition" to the next year's Championship Circuit and thanked Scott Lingrell for running the first Classic tournament at DecipherCon.<ref name="pcf-360-5124">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5124#5124 Player's Committee Announces Winter Contest], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318152804/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5124%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He explained that Brangus Glee was banned because, with [[Set Your Course For Alderaan / The Ultimate Power In The Universe|Set Your Course For Alderaan]] (which pulls the Death Star docking bay) and [[Put All Sections On Alert]], a deck could take any card it wanted from its Lost Pile into hand all game, and that Ketwol was banned so that the Light Side would not keep a similar deck built on [[A New Secret Base]] and [[On The Edge]].<ref name="pcf-359-5173">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5173#5173 Player's Committee Announces Winter Contest], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318153123/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5176%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

The 2003 Championship Circuit was the first to include Closed Environment events, with Classic Format events at the top of the list.<ref name="pc-waclassic" /> In 2003 several Championship Circuit events were played in Classic: the California, Ohio and Virginia State Championships and the United Kingdom National Championship,<ref name="pc-us03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040622065452/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/usevents.htm State Championships (US Events)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 22 June 2004.</ref><ref name="pc-intl03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040621085705/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/intlevents.htm Nationals and Provincials (International Events)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 21 June 2004.</ref> a Classic Format Open Qualifier in Vancouver, Washington, on 2 August 2003,<ref name="pc-waclassic">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809112718/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/WAclassicopen06122003.htm Classic Format Open Qualifier, Vancouver, WA], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref> and one of the two Day 1 qualifiers of the [[2003 World Championship]].<ref name="pc-wc03sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040620165803/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/worldchamps06122003.htm SWCCG World Championships Coming to Atlanta!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 20 June 2004.</ref>

Howard wrote on 29 March 2003 that Operatives, banned in Classic at first, were no longer banned.<ref name="pcf-1219-22719">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=22719#22719 Operatives], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (29 March 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040819025306/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1219%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In May 2003 the Players Committee's new (V) Starting Effects for Classic let a player lose 2 Force to play a Defensive Shield; players had seen their spoilers thanks to [[Greg Zinn]],<ref name="pcf-1487-26155">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=26155#26155 New Starting Effects for Classic], Uriah Watkins, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040126055136/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1487%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> who pointed out that because the Light Side and Dark Side (V) Starting Effects have different titles, the forfeit −3 of each applies to characters hit by an EPP weapon, for forfeit −6 in all.<ref name="pcf-1487-26163">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=26163#26163 New Starting Effects for Classic], Greg Zinn, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (16 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040126055136/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1487%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In August 2003 a player posting as Sithborg explained that the Defensive Shields themselves had never been banned in Classic, only the original Starting Effects, and that Classic now had a Starting Effect from which they could be played.<ref name="pcf-377-31333">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31333#31333 What strategies are mostly viable in classic?], Sithborg, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041217215857/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34439%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[Chris Wodicka]] wrote that [[Damian Loback]] had won the Classic tournament at [[Gen Con 2003]] with [[Massassi Base Operations / One In A Million|Massassi Base Operations]],<ref name="pcf-377-31335">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31335#31335 What strategies are mostly viable in classic?], Chris Wodicka, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041217215857/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34439%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and a player posting as elvis solo wrote on 16 October 2003 that he had won the Classic Day 1 qualifier of the [[2003 World Championship]] at Dragon*Con with [[You Can Either Profit By This... / Or Be Destroyed|Profit]] and [[This Deal Is Getting Worse All The Time / Pray I Don't Alter It Any Further|This Deal Is Getting Worse All The Time]], beating Loback's deck.<ref name="pcf-377-34439">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34439#34439 What strategies are mostly viable in classic?], elvis solo, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (16 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041217215857/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34439%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 7 July 2003 Howard confirmed that Classic had always included all Virtual Cards, not only Virtual Sets 1–3.<ref name="pcf-1911-30439">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30439#30439 Has Classic Format expanded to include VSets 4 and 5?  (nt)], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040327232218/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30461%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> After Howard said at Dragon*Con 2003 that "insert" cards were legal in Classic, the official Classic ban list was changed to match, as [[Nick Kolnik]] reported on 18 September 2003.<ref name="pcf-2197-33349">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349#33349 Are inserts allowed classic], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 20 September 2003 Howard wrote that he was no longer part of the Classic decision-making process,<ref name="pcf-2197-33412">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33412#33412 Are inserts allowed classic], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (20 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and Kolnik pointed players to an Advocate-led discussion of possible changes to the format on TheForce.Net's SW:CCG forum.<ref name="pcf-2197-33419">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33419#33419 Are inserts allowed classic], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (20 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041228093631/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=48905%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

Watch Your Step remained banned. [[Chris Wodicka]] explained in May 2003 that almost every deck lost something under the Classic restrictions (Hunt Down decks, for example, lost "Maul" and "R3 Fett"), while a Watch Your Step deck lost only cards such as [[Phylo Gandish|Phylo]] and [[Chewie, Enraged]].<ref name="pcf-1554-27139">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=27139#27139 Why was "Watch your step..." banned in classic? al], Chris Wodicka, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040122124945/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31095%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Howard wrote on 23 June 2003 that Watch Your Step was not balanced in Classic because the Dark Side lacked other "meta" choices, and that it might be allowed back in the future, "but not with the current scene".<ref name="pcf-1554-29863">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=29863#29863 Why was "Watch your step..." banned in classic? al], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (23 June 2003). * [[Classic (no v-cards) (Modified)]] (<code>classic_no_virtual_m</code>) &mdash; Decipher cards only, with 14 Defensive Shields allowed.<ref name="gemp" />
